title: Wampum belts presented; Northfield towers proposal reviewed
subtitle: Source protection plan update, bike theft concerns, and community shoutouts for Pride Month and local award winners.
overview: Council received three replica Wampum belts commissioned by the City in the spirit of reconciliation, during Indigenous History Month. Council also supported technical updates to the Grand River Source Protection Plan that apply within Waterloo {{vote:m2}}. The updates reflect changes to protection areas around municipal wells, including two replacement wells and a new well planned by the Region.

Council held an informal public meeting on a proposed Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment for the Northfield Drive and Weber Street North lands. The proposal would allow high-density residential towers alongside employment uses on a site now zoned for employment. No decision was made. Staff will review the issues and report back, and a formal public meeting will follow. One councillor left the room for this item after declaring a conflict.

A resident also asked Council to take bike theft more seriously, including through a partnership with Project 529. Council met in closed session earlier in the afternoon on training, legal advice and litigation matters, including Ontario Land Tribunal updates. The minutes report no public decisions from it.

decisions.item: Grand River Source Protection Plan update
decisions.detail: Council approved report IPPW2024-029 and supported the proposed technical updates to the Grand River Source Protection Plan that apply within Waterloo {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Councillors asked staff why parcels were added to or removed from source protection areas. Staff said protection areas are concentric zones around wells based on sensitivity and travel time, and were reconfigured because of the Region's replacement and new wells. Public consultation is led by the source protection committee, with the Region as municipal lead.

On the Northfield proposal, councillors and a resident delegate raised traffic. They cited long queues on Northfield Drive from LRT signal timing, the pedestrian crossing, and congestion on the Expressway. The delegate suggested grade separation and road changes. Staff said the Region will review the traffic study and that signal timing is ongoing work.

Councillors questioned the proposed cut in landscaped open space from 30% to 15% on the residential portion. The applicant's planner said the open space would be concentrated into programmed public spaces rather than perimeter landscaping. Other questions covered schools, child care, affordable housing and energy systems.
A second resident spoke in support, citing regional population growth and the need for housing. That resident asked for fewer parking spaces, more green space and purpose-built rental units.

The resident who spoke on bike theft said the library's main branch had no outdoor cameras and urged Waterloo Regional Police to work with Project 529. Councillors shared their own experiences. One said Waterloo's bike lockers work well and should be expanded, and another said the Region has been in contact with Project 529.
